{{Term/Store|Nabooru||Series, OoT, OoT3D}} (pronounced {{IPA|nəˈbɔər.uː}} {{Respell|nə|BOAR|oo}}<ref name="BotW Urbosa"/>) is a recurring character in {{TLoZ Series}}.{{Exp Game|OoT, OoT3D}}<ref name="E 239"/>{{Name Ref|BotW}} She is the second-in-command of the [[Gerudo]], [[Ganondorf]] being her only superior. She has a second-in-command herself.<ref name="OoT Gerudo Warrior"/> Nabooru is highly respected by the other Gerudo,<ref name="OoT Koume"/> who are unaware of her rebellion against Ganondorf. During the events of {{OoT|-}}, she becomes the new [[Sage of Spirit]] and aids [[Link]] in his battle against Ganon.

==Biography==
==={{OoT|-}}===
[[Link]] meets Nabooru in the [[Spirit Temple (Ocarina of Time)|Spirit Temple]] as a child, having used the "[[Requiem of Spirit]]", which he learned in the future, to reach the [[Desert Colossus]]. At this time, Nabooru is already in opposition to Ganondorf's behavior.<ref name="OoT Nabooru"/> She intends to infiltrate Ganon's followers' headquarters there, but is unable to without the [[Silver Gauntlets]], which are out of reach beyond a very small opening.<ref name="OoT Nabooru 2"/> She asks Link to get the gauntlets for her, promising to "do something great" for him in return.<ref name="OoT Nabooru 3"/> Once Link acquires the Silver Gauntlets, [[Koume]] and [[Kotake]] discover and capture Nabooru.<ref name="OoT Nabooru 4"/> 

When Link returns to the temple as an adult, Nabooru has been brainwashed.<ref name="OoT Koume 2"/> While brainwashed, Nabooru was used to lead activities contrary to the values she previously held.<ref name="OoT Carpenter"/> During this intervening period, Nabooru is apparently rumored to brainwash people herself.<ref name="OoT Carpenter 2"/>

Toward the end of the Spirit Temple, Link confronts Kotake and Koume, apparently fussing over a strange [[Iron Knuckle (Boss)|Iron Knuckle]].<ref name="OoT Navi"/> They command it to attack him and vanish. Upon its defeat, the Iron Knuckle's armor falls off to reveal Nabooru with the spell lifted. Kotake and Koume reappear and capture her a second time before retreating to the boss room ahead.<ref name="OoT Koume 2"/><ref name="OoT Koume"/><ref name="OoT Kotake"/><ref name="OoT Kotake 2"/> After their defeat, Nabooru is freed and she awakens as the [[Sage of Spirit]], giving Link the [[Spirit Medallion]].<ref name="OoT Nabooru 5"/><ref name="OoT Nabooru 6"/><ref name="OoT Spirit Medallion"/>

When Link defeats Ganon, Nabooru and the other Sages combine their powers to seal Ganon away. During the ending, she can be seen overlooking a celebrating [[Hyrule]] on [[Death Mountain]] with the other Sages.

==={{BotW|-}}===
In ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild|Breath of the Wild]]'', the [[Divine Beast Vah Naboris]] is named in honor of Nabooru.<ref name="BotW Urbosa 2"/>

==Other Appearances==
==={{OoT|-}} (Himekawa)===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
In the {{OoT (Himekawa)}}, Nabooru's role is slightly different from the game. She is under the influence of Koume and Kotake as well, but is not transformed into an Iron Knuckle. She is sent to spy on [[Sheik]] which results in her combating Link. He then frees her from the influence which allows her to help release the other Gerudo. She also gives Link the [[Mirror Shield]], which she claims she stole a while back.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) vol.2 60"/> After [[Princess Zelda]] is captured by Ganondorf, Nabooru explains that the Gerudo race consists only of women, and that the first male born after one hundred years has the right to be chief. Nabooru decides to fight Ganondorf with Link, commenting that there are some things even a master thief should never steal.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) vol.2 69"/> After the two battle monsters, [[Rauru]] speaks with both Link and Nabooru, revealing that Nabooru has been awakened as the [[Sage of Spirit]].<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) vol.2 71"/> Together the sages, including Nabooru, create a bridge to Ganondorf's castle. 
{{Noncanon|End}}

==Trivia==
*{{OoT|-}} contains unused text from Nabooru, wherein she remarks that Link is an enemy of Ganondorf and must die.<ref name="OoT Nabooru 7"/> This dialogue was probably to be used when fighting her as an Iron Knuckle.
*In {{TWW}}, one of the stained glass windows in [[Hyrule Castle]]'s basement depicts Nabooru along with the other Sages from {{OoT|-}}.
*Nabooru's in-game clothing is colored white, despite being shown as pink in the official artwork.
* In {{BotW|-}} and {{TotK|-}}, [[Mount Nabooru]] and the [[Mount Nabooru Well]] in the [[Gerudo Highlands]] are named after Nabooru.<ref name="BotW Piggyback 351"/> In {{TotK|-}}, they are joined by the [[Mount Nabooru Cave]], the [[Mount Nabooru South Cave]], and the [[Nabooru Canyon Mine]].

==Nomenclature==
Nabooru's name, like several other characters from {{OoT|-}}, is taken from a [[Nabooru Town|Town]] in {{TAoL}}.
{{Nomenclature}}
